headline: WhatsApp Web extends voice and video calls to group chats
summary: The popular messaging app is testing group calling functionality for its web client, bringing it closer to feature parity with its mobile counterparts.
details: WhatsApp is currently testing a new feature that will allow users to participate in voice and video calls within group chats directly from WhatsApp Web.
This functionality has been a long-requested feature for desktop users, who have previously only been able to make one-on-one calls via the web interface.
The expansion of group calling to the web version aims to provide a more seamless and integrated communication experience for users who prefer using WhatsApp on their computers.
While the feature is still in its testing phase, its eventual rollout is expected to significantly enhance the utility of WhatsApp Web for both personal and professional communication.
caption:
WhatsApp Web is getting a major upgrade: group voice and video calls are now in testing.

WhatsApp is currently testing a new feature that will allow users to participate in voice and video calls within group chats directly from WhatsApp Web.

This functionality has been a long-requested feature for desktop users, who have previously only been able to make one-on-one calls via the web interface.

The expansion of group calling to the web version aims to provide a more seamless and integrated communication experience for users who prefer using WhatsApp on their computers.

While the feature is still in its testing phase, its eventual rollout is expected to significantly enhance the utility of WhatsApp Web for both personal and professional communication.

headline: Meta CTO Andrew Bosworth Calls AI Reorg 'Atrocious'
summary: Meta's CTO admits the company botched its AI division rollout, promising better communication and career support for engineers.
details: Meta's Chief Technology Officer Andrew Bosworth has acknowledged that the company's recent reorganization of its Applied AI division was handled poorly, describing the rollout as 'atrocious'. This admission comes in response to internal reports of widespread dissatisfaction among the approximately 6,500 engineers and product managers assigned to the unit.

Employees within the Applied AI division reportedly felt the work was menial, with one describing the environment as a 'gulag.' Bosworth admitted that Meta undermined employees' trust regarding the value of their expertise, career advancement, and potential for impact. The rapid strategic shifts and hiring fluctuations also left teams feeling unstable.

To address the unrest, Bosworth stated that Meta plans to provide more personalized attention to employees. This includes capping managers at around 20 direct reports and minimizing frequent team restructurings. Leadership will also commit to clearer explanations for strategic and organizational changes.

Maher Saba, a vice president leading the Applied AI team, has informed employees that they will now be permitted to seek and transfer to other roles within Meta if they can secure them. This move aims to restore a sense of agency and allow employees to pursue roles that better align with their interests.

While Bosworth emphasized that AI is unlikely to fully replace human workers, he cautioned that 'AI won’t take your job but someone who knows AI might.' He also noted that there will be difficult trade-offs regarding compute resources for AI tools, promising transparency and responsible investment to mitigate bottlenecks.

In an effort to improve morale, Bosworth pledged to make Meta a more 'fun and enjoyable' workplace. Plans include enhancing office break areas with better snacks and drinks, increasing travel budgets, and organizing more social events to foster in-person connections among employees.
